Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: relatedStructure
candidates.comment: A related structure relation between an anatomical system and structures that connect to or are associated with it, but are not part of the system itself. Also called associated structure, connected structure. Examples: "The circulatory system has a related structure 'the heart'.", "The nervous system has a related structure 'the brain'.", "The digestive system has a related structure 'the liver'."

relations.embedding_query_text: triggered_by: Caused or initiated by a preceding event

chosen_property.label: source

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: byMonth
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: previousStartDate

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. candidates.label: scheduledTime

candidates.label: jobStartDate

A job posting has a jobStartDate of 'as soon as possible'. Distinct from jobImmediateStart, which is a boolean flag for immediate availability.

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". candidates.label: coverageStartTime

candidates.label: scheduledPaymentDate
candidates.comment: The specific date on which an invoice is planned or expected to be paid. Also called payment due date, invoice due date, planned payment date. Distinct from `paymentDueDate`, which is a more general term for when payment is due.

candidates.label: applicationStartDate
candidates.comment: An application start date relation between an educational or occupational program and the date when it begins accepting applications for an enrollment cycle. Also called application opening date, submission start date. Examples: "A university program's application start date is '2022-09-01'.", "The scholarship program's application start date is 'January 1st'."

candidates.label: availabilityStarts
candidates.comment: A date or time marking the beginning of availability for a product or service in an offer or access specification. Also called: availability start date, offer start, access start time. Examples: "Offer 'New Product' availabilityStarts '2023-11-01'", "ActionAccessSpecification 'Pre-sale' availabilityStarts '2023-10-20T09:00:00'". Distinct from availabilityEnds, which marks the end.

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: estimatedFlightDuration

candidates.label: timeToComplete
candidates.comment: A duration representing the expected length of time to complete an educational or occupational program when attending full-time. Also called "program duration", "completion duration", "full-time study length", "expected completion time". Examples: "The degree program has timeToComplete 4 years", "The certification's timeToComplete is 6 months", "This program requires timeToComplete 2 years of full-time study."

candidates.label: departureTime
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a trip and its expected departure time. Also called: scheduled departure, leaving time, takeoff time. Examples: "Flight" departure time "2023-11-01T08:00:00Z", "Bus Trip" departure time "14:30:00", "Train Journey" departure time "2023-12-25T10:00:00". candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: timeRequired
candidates.comment: A duration representing the approximate time typically needed for an audience to engage with or complete a creative work. Examples: "The article has timeRequired 10 minutes", "The course's timeRequired is 40 hours", "This creative work takes timeRequired 2 hours to watch."

candidates.label: activityDuration
candidates.comment: An activity duration relation between an exercise plan and the length of time recommended for engaging in the activity. Also called exercise length, workout time, session duration. Examples: "An exercise plan's activity duration is '30 minutes'.", "The yoga routine's activity duration is '1 hour'."

candidates.label: arrivalTime
candidates.comment: An expected time of arrival for a trip. Also called: estimated arrival, scheduled arrival, landing time. Examples: "Trip to NYC arrivalTime '2023-10-27T14:30:00'", "Flight 789 arrivalTime '18:00'", "Bus Trip arrivalTime 'tomorrow 09:15'."

candidates.label: deliveryTime
candidates.comment: A temporal duration relation between delivery time settings or offer shipping details and the total delay from order receipt to goods reaching the final customer. Also called: total delivery time, shipping duration, estimated delivery. Examples: "Standard Shipping" delivery time "5-7 business days", "Express Delivery" delivery time "1-2 days", "International Shipment" delivery time "2-3 weeks". Distinct from deliveryLeadTime, which is the time until dispatch or pickup readiness.

candidates.label: jobDuration
candidates.comment: An employment term relation between a job posting and the expected length of the employment period. A job posting has a jobDuration of 'seasonal'.

candidates.label: suggestedAnswer

candidates.label: legislationLegalValue

candidates.label: eligibilityToWorkRequirement

candidates.label: legislationLegalForce

candidates.label: acceptedAnswer

candidates.label: legislationJurisdiction

candidates.label: legalName

candidates.label: dateCreated

candidates.label: copyrightYear

candidates.label: dateline

candidates.label: uploadDate

candidates.label: area
candidates.comment: An area relation between a broadcast service and the geographic place where its users can access it. Also called service region, coverage area, broadcast zone. Examples: "A radio station's area is 'Greater London'.", "The TV service's area is 'North America'."

relations.embedding_query_text: caused_by: Directly responsible for an event

chosen_property.label: source
chosen_property.justification: Schema.org 'source' links an event to its causal origin, fitting a murder caused by a person.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: cause
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical condition and its medical cause. Also called "etiology", "origin", "caused by". Examples: "Flu medical condition cause Influenza virus", "Heart attack medical condition cause Coronary artery disease". Distinct from causeOf, which describes what a medical cause leads to, whereas cause describes what leads to a condition.

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: organizer
candidates.comment: An organization or person responsible for organizing an event. Also called event planner, host, coordinator, promoter. Examples: "Conference X organizer 'Acme Events Inc.'", "Concert Y organizer 'Live Nation'", "Workshop Z organizer 'Jane Doe'". Distinct from performer, who participates in the event.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: legislationResponsible
candidates.comment: A responsibility relation between a piece of legislation and the individual or organization accountable for its elaboration or inquiries. Also called: responsible for, overseen by, managed by. Examples: "Health Act legislationResponsible Ministry of Health", "Environmental Law legislationResponsible EPA", "Tax Reform legislationResponsible Treasury Department". Distinct from legislationPassedBy, which refers to the original enacting authority.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

relations.embedding_query_text: member_of: Belongs to a group or organization

chosen_property.label: memberOf
chosen_property.justification: Schema.org 'memberOf' directly links a person to an organization they belong to.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: musicGroupMember
candidates.comment: A person who is a member of a music group. Also called band member, group member, musician in group. Examples: "The Beatles musicGroupMember 'John Lennon'", "Queen musicGroupMember 'Freddie Mercury'", "Fleetwood Mac musicGroupMember 'Stevie Nicks'". Distinct from member, which is a general property for any organization.

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: owns
candidates.comment: A thing that is owned by an organization or person. Also called possesses, holds title to, has ownership of. Examples: "John Doe owns 'a car'", "Acme Corp owns 'a patent'", "Sarah owns 'her house'". Distinct from memberOf, which describes membership in a group.

candidates.label: hasMemberProgram
candidates.comment: A member program relation between an organization and a member program it offers. Also called offers program, loyalty program, membership program. Examples: "An airline has a member program for frequent flyers.", "An eCommerce merchant has a member program for discounts.", "The organization offers a member program."

candidates.label: parentOrganization
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between an organization and the larger organization it belongs to. Also called belongs to, is a division of, is a subsidiary of, is part of. Examples: Google is a parent organization of YouTube. A local branch is a parent organization of its national headquarters. A department is a parent organization of its university. Distinct from subOrganization, which points from a larger organization to its smaller components.

candidates.label: hostingOrganization
candidates.comment: A hosting organization relation between a member program or program membership and the organization that offers or manages it. Also called program provider, membership organization, host company. Examples: "A member program has a hosting organization 'Airline X'.", "The program membership is with a hosting organization.", "This program is hosted by a specific organization."

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

chosen_property.label: basedOnSelfIncrimination
chosen_property.definition: An event that is based on a self-incrimination account or interview
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property for an event based on self-incrimination; 'isBasedOn' applies to creative works, not legal events.

candidates.label: isBasedOn
candidates.comment: A derivation relation between a creative work and the resource (another work, product, or URL) from which it is adapted or modified. Also called derived from, adapted from, based on, inspired by, modification of. Examples: A movie isBasedOn 'a novel'. A software update isBasedOn 'previous version'. A remix isBasedOn 'original song'. Distinct from isBasedOnUrl, which specifically points to a URL as the source.

candidates.label: recordingOf
candidates.comment: A recording of relation between a music recording and the music composition it represents. Also called rendition of, version of, based on composition. Examples: "A music recording 'Bohemian Rhapsody' is a recording of 'the Queen composition'.", "A classical track is a recording of 'Beethoven's Symphony No. 9'.", "A cover song is a recording of 'the original composition'.". Distinct from recordedAs, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: isBasedOnUrl
candidates.comment: A source URL relation between a creative work and a specific URL that served as a resource for its creation. Also called source URL, derived from URL, based on URL, reference URL. Examples: A research paper has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://arxiv.org/abs/1234.5678'. A blog post has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://example.com/original-article'. A web page has an isBasedOnUrl of 'https://old-version.com/page'. Distinct from isBasedOn, which can refer to any CreativeWork or Product, not just a URL.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: dateCreated
candidates.comment: A temporal origin relation between a creative work or data feed item and the date it was created or added. Also called: creation date, date of origin, initial date. Examples: "Painting" date created "1889-05-01", "Blog Post" date created "2023-03-15T10:00:00Z", "Data Feed Entry" date created "2023-01-01". Distinct from datePublished, which is the date of first public release.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: causeOf
candidates.comment: A causal relation between a medical cause and the medical entity (condition, complication, symptom) it produces. Also called "results in", "leads to", "produces". Examples: "Influenza virus medical causeOf Flu", "Smoking medical causeOf Lung cancer". Distinct from cause, which describes what leads to a condition, whereas causeOf describes what a medical cause leads to.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

chosen_property.label: inVehicle
chosen_property.definition: A person's presence in a vehicle during an event
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property for a person in a vehicle; existing properties focus on vehicle attributes.

candidates.label: vehicleEngine
candidates.comment: A vehicle engine relation between a vehicle and information about its engine(s). Also called engine details, motor specification, power unit. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleEngine 'V8 engine'", "Vehicle vehicleEngine 'Electric motor'", "Vehicle vehicleEngine '2.0L Turbocharged'".

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: bodyType
candidates.comment: A qualitative value, text, or URL indicating the design and body style of a vehicle. Also called: vehicle style, car type, chassis type. Examples: "Vehicle 'Ford Focus' bodyType 'Hatchback'", "Vehicle 'Mercedes C-Class' bodyType 'Sedan'."

candidates.label: vehicleInteriorColor
candidates.comment: A vehicle interior color relation between a vehicle and the color or color combination of its interior. Also called interior color, cabin color, upholstery color. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleInteriorColor 'Black'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorColor 'Beige Leather'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorColor 'Grey Fabric'".

candidates.label: vehicleIdentificationNumber
candidates.comment: A vehicle identification number relation between a vehicle and its unique serial number (VIN). Also called VIN, chassis number, serial number. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleIdentificationNumber '1G1AP52W691XXXXXX'", "Car vehicleIdentificationNumber 'JTDKN31V60JXXXXXX'", "Truck vehicleIdentificationNumber '3FAHP000000XXXXXX'".

candidates.label: vehicleInteriorType
candidates.comment: A vehicle interior type relation between a vehicle and the type or material of its interior. Also called interior material, upholstery type, cabin trim. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'leather'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'synthetic fabric'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'wood trim'".

candidates.label: vehicleConfiguration
candidates.comment: A vehicle configuration relation between a vehicle and a short text describing its specific setup. Also called vehicle setup, car configuration, model description. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleConfiguration '5dr hatchback ST 2.5 MT 225 hp'", "Vehicle vehicleConfiguration 'limited edition'", "Vehicle vehicleConfiguration 'AWD, leather seats'".

candidates.label: speed
candidates.comment: A quantitative value representing the speed range of a vehicle. Also called "vehicle speed", "maximum speed", "speed capability", "velocity range". Examples: "The car has speed 200 KMH", "The boat's speed is 30 knots", "This vehicle's speed range is 0-120 mph."

candidates.label: vehicleSeatingCapacity
candidates.comment: A vehicle seating capacity relation between a vehicle and the number of passengers it can seat. Also called seating capacity, passenger capacity, number of seats. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '5'", "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '7 persons'", "Vehicle vehicleSeatingCapacity '2'".

candidates.label: vehicleTransmission
candidates.comment: A vehicle transmission relation between a vehicle and the type of component used for transmitting power to the wheels. Also called transmission type, gearbox type, drivetrain. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Automatic'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Manual'", "Vehicle vehicleTransmission 'Continuously Variable Transmission'".

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: permitAudience
candidates.comment: A targeting relation between a permit and the specific audience it is intended for. Also called target group, eligible recipients, intended users. Examples: A fishing permit has a permit audience of 'Local Residents'. A building permit has a permit audience of 'Licensed Contractors'. A student permit has a permit audience of 'University Students'.

candidates.label: potentialUse
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the intended use of a chemical substance or molecular entity by humans. Also called intended application, human use, purpose. Examples: A chemical substance has a potential use as 'fertilizer'. A molecular entity has a potential use as 'drug component'. The compound has a potential use in 'food preservation'.

candidates.label: recipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation between an action (like sending or paying) and the audience, contact point, organization, or person receiving it. Also called receiver, intended for, sent to. Examples: "A message has a recipient 'John Doe'.", "A donation has a recipient 'Charity Organization'.", "A payment has a recipient 'Vendor Inc.'."

candidates.label: providesService
candidates.comment: A service provision relation between a service channel and the specific service it delivers. Also called channel delivers, service offered via, offers service. Examples: "An online portal provides service 'customer support'.", "A phone line provides service 'technical assistance'.", "A mobile app provides service 'online banking'."

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: lender
candidates.comment: A lending participant relation between a borrow action and the person or organization providing the object being borrowed. Also called: loan provider, creditor, financing entity. Examples: "BorrowAction lender Bank of America", "BorrowAction lender John Doe", "BorrowAction lender Library".

candidates.label: suggestedGender
candidates.comment: An indication of the recommended gender for an intended person or audience. Also called "target gender", "audience gender", "gender recommendation". Examples: "The clothing item has suggestedGender unisex", "The audience specification includes suggestedGender female", "This product is for suggestedGender male."

candidates.label: sender
candidates.comment: The audience, organization, or person initiating and transmitting a message or action. Also called originator, dispatcher, message source, sender of message. Examples: `Email Message` sender `John Doe`, `ReceiveAction` sender `Customer Service`, `Broadcast Message` sender `News Organization`. Distinct from `recipient`, which is the receiving party.

candidates.label: recordedIn
candidates.comment: A recording capture relation between an event and the creative work that captured all or part of it. Also called captured by, documented in, featured in. Examples: "A concert event was recorded in 'a live album'.", "A historical event was recorded in 'a documentary film'.", "A speech event was recorded in 'a news broadcast'.". Distinct from recordedAt, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: observationAbout
candidates.comment: An entity, often a place, that an observation is about or associated with. Also called observed entity, subject of observation, related to observation. Examples: "Weather Observation observationAbout 'London'", "Patient Vitals Observation observationAbout 'John Doe'", "Traffic Count Observation observationAbout 'Main Street'".

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: confirmationNumber
candidates.comment: An identification relation for an invoice or order, providing a number that confirms its receipt. Also called "order confirmation", "booking reference", "receipt number". Examples: "Online order confirmationNumber 'ABC-12345'", "Flight invoice confirmationNumber 'XYZ-67890'".

candidates.label: studySubject
candidates.comment: An investigative relation between a medical study and the medical entity (condition, therapy, drug, etc.) that is being investigated. Also called "subject of investigation", "research focus", "entity studied", "trial subject". Examples: "The medical study has studySubject a new drug", "The clinical trial's studySubject is a specific medical condition", "This study investigates a studySubject therapy."

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.
